title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation & QBR Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It covers the technical integration checklist, escalation matrix and runbook references, known issues and workarounds relevant to new customers, and the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) / health-check templates used by Customer Success. Use this document as the canonical guide for onboarding, day-1 support expectations, and the first 90 days of adoption.

Scope:
- New enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private deployments) and large Hosted customers moving to production.
- Cross-functional owners: Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Support (Tier 1–3), Product, and Eng-SRE.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-value by standardizing integration steps and required artifacts.
- Ensure fast, consistent incident handling via a clear escalation matrix.
- Provide repeatable QBR/health-check templates tied to SLOs and product metrics.

Ownership and Roles

Primary contacts:
- Customer Success Manager (CSM) — onboarding owner, relationship & QBRs.
- Solutions Engineer (SE) — integration lead, API/samples, proofs-of-concept.
- Support (Tier 1) — first-line support for operational questions.
- Eng-SRE (on-call) — handles platform incidents impacting customer SLA.

Role responsibilities (summary):
- CSM: coordinate kickoff, business goals, success criteria, schedule QBRs.
- SE: complete integration checklist, provide sample prompts, validate performance targets.
- Support: triage support requests within SLAs and escalate per matrix.
- Eng-SRE: own production incidents, root cause analysis, and postmortems.

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (to complete before Day 0)

1) Contract & Access
   - Signed MSA and SSO/KMS paperwork completed.
   - Seats and RBAC roles provisioned in Console.
   - API keys and audit logging enabled for the customer account.

2) Environment & Networking (Private/Dedicated)
   - Network requirements validated (IP allowlist, VPC peering, firewall rules).
   - Certificate and KMS/HSM details exchanged and tested.
   - Capacity profile agreed (concurrency, expected TPS, burst windows).

3) Security & Compliance
   - Data residency and retention policies confirmed.
   - Logging and audit stream endpoint configured and tested.

4) Success Criteria & Metrics
   - Define 0–30 and 30–90 day success metrics (e.g., 95th pct latency target, error rate <0.5%, cost per 1k tokens).

Integration Guide (basic sequence for SEs)

Step 1 — Kickoff and scope  
- Run kickoff with customer: use the integration checklist template and confirm SLAs, traffic patterns, and security needs.

Step 2 — Provisioning  
- Create customer-specific project in Console and provision keys.
- Configure RBAC roles and auditing.

Step 3 — API integration (sample)  
- Provide sample SDK snippet and curl example: 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-2-medium","prompt":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

- Recommend SDK usage for streaming and function calling.

Step 4 — Load & perf validation  
- Run load tests with representative prompts. Targets to validate: p95 latency <= agreed threshold, error rate <0.5% under steady-state load.
- Capture token distribution and average request size; share cost projection.

Step 5 — Observability & Tracing  
- Enable per-route telemetry and tracing hooks.
- Confirm log forwarding to customer SIEM if requested.

Step 6 — Cutover & Canary  
- Perform canary rollout (10–20% traffic) for 24–48 hours.
- Observe latency, errors, and quality regressions; rollback criteria: sustained error surge or p99 latency > 2x baseline.

Operational SLAs and Support Process

Support tiers and targets:
- Tier 1 (Support): initial triage, business hours response SLA = 30 minutes for P1, 4 hours for P2, 1 business day for P3.
- Tier 2 (Solutions / Platform SME): deep triage and customer-facing remediation, response within 4 hours for P1 escalations.
- Tier 3 (Eng-SRE / Product): code-level or infra fixes, on-call engagement per incident.

Severity classification (guideline):
1) P1 — Production outage / customer unable to serve traffic (SLA breach imminent).
2) P2 — Degraded performance impacting user experience (e.g., high latency, elevated error rates).
3) P3 — Non-urgent functional issues, integration questions, or feature requests.

Support request workflow (numbered):
1. Customer opens ticket via Support portal / email / Slack.
2. Tier 1 triages and gathers logs (request traces, request IDs, timestamps, model and route names).
3. If triage indicates infrastructure/bug root cause, Tier 1 escalates to Tier 2 with collected artifacts.
4. Tier 2 engages Eng-SRE for P1/P2 and updates customer every 30–60 minutes for P1 until resolved.
5. Post-incident: create incident report and link to customer’s account page; schedule RCA if P1.

Escalation Matrix (contacts & timing)

- Tier 1 Support: support@redwood-inference.example (Business hours) — 30 min initial response.
- SE on-call: se-oncall@redwood-inference.example — escalation within 60 minutes for unrecoverable P2.
- Eng-SRE on-call: pager, Slack #sre-oncall — immediate engagement for P1.
- CSM: notify within 1 hour for any P1 affecting SLA or >4 hour P2 impacts.

Escalation steps (explicit):
1) Tier 1 identifies P1 and notifies SE and Eng-SRE via pager; create internal incident channel.
2) Eng-SRE triages and determines mitigation (traffic reroute, model fallback, capacity scaling).
3) If mitigation is unavailable, follow rollback/cutover plan and update customer with ETA.

Known Issues and Workarounds (frequent items)

- Issue: Intermittent 5xx errors when KV cache contention spikes.
  Workaround: Temporarily switch to smaller batch size and enable immediate prefix caching. SE action: open support ticket with cache metrics and request Eng-SRE cache tuning.

- Issue: Higher-than-expected token costs from verbose system prompts.
  Workaround: Move static instructions to metadata / context window trimming and use shorter system-level prompts. Provide prompt engineering guide to customer.

- Issue: TLS handshake failures in Private deployments when mutual-TLS certs expire.
  Workaround: Validate cert rotation schedule; if expired, follow rollback to alternate gateway and apply emergency cert renewal steps (see Eng-Private-Deployments runbook).

- Issue: Embeddings semantic drift after quantized model rollout.
  Workaround: Pin customer to previous model variant and schedule controlled re-quantization with regression tests.

For each known issue include: detection signal, immediate mitigation, owner, and follow-up action. Keep this section up to date with links to incident reports.

QBR and Health-Check Template

Cadence:
- First QBR: 30 days post-production.
- Subsequent: Quarterly (or monthly for high-touch enterprise).

QBR agenda (standard 60–90 minutes):
1) Executive summary: adoption highlights, business outcomes, and topline metrics.
2) Reliability & SLA review: uptime % (last quarter), incidents (P1/P2/P3), open action items.
3) Performance & cost: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, cost per 1M tokens, billing anomalies.
4) Product usage & trends: top routes, model variants, and feature adoption (streaming, function calling).
5) Roadmap & requests: product improvements, integration requests, prioritization.
6) Action plan: owners, milestones, and success criteria for next quarter.

Health-check checklist (30–60 minute technical review):
- Confirm key SLOs: p99 latency target, error rate thresholds, and availability.
- Review telemetry: tail latency spikes, rate-limiting events, cache hit ratio, and retries.
- Verify cost alignment: token distribution and unexpected usage patterns.
- Security review: audit logs, KMS rotations, and access logs.

QBR Report artifacts (deliverables):
- One-pager executive summary (PDF).
- Technical appendix: graphs for latency, errors, and top endpoints (PNG/CSV).
- Action items tracker: owner, due date, status.

Postmortem & RCA Expectations

- For any P1 incident impacting an enterprise customer, produce an RCA within 5 business days.
- RCA should include timeline, root cause, mitigations applied, long-term fixes, and post-RCA sign-off by Eng-SRE and Product.

Templates and Attachments

- Integration checklist (copyable): a table of required artifacts, responsible party, and status (NOT STARTED / IN PROGRESS / DONE).
- QBR slide deck template (link to shared drive).
- Incident report template (link to incident management system).

Appendix: Useful commands & troubleshooting snippets

- Retrieve request logs (example):
  awslogs get /redwood/customer-account --start="2027-07-01T00:00:00Z" --end="2027-07-01T01:00:00Z" --filter "request_id:abcd1234"

- Example rollout rollback command (internal):
  rh rollout undo --app redwood-serving --to-revision=20270710-rc2 --namespace=customer-123

- Contact list (internal):
  - CSM: maya.chen@redwood-inference.example
  - SE lead: alejandro.ruiz@redwood-inference.example
  - SRE on-call: see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks for calendar and pager escalation.

Maintenance and doc lifecycle

- Owner: Customer Success (Maya Chen).
- Review cadence: annual review minimum; update after any P1 affecting playbook content.
- Change log: document major changes to integration steps or escalation contacts in the top of this doc.

This playbook is a living document. SEs and Support should add post-implementation learnings (e.g., common integration pitfalls) and sample prompts that improved cost/latency tradeoffs.
